question: A new hire logs in through SSO for the first time. What role does she get, and does she use up one of our member seats?
reference_answer: If she has no existing match, a new user is created automatically in the team matching her email domain with the Viewer role by default, which you can change. SSO users count towards the team member limit, so no new users can be added at the limit.
key_facts: New SSO users get the Viewer role by default
SSO users count toward the team member limit
answer: By default, new members who log in through SSO are assigned the Viewer role [1]. Additionally, SSO users count towards your team member limit [1].

citations.quote: By default, new members are assigned the Viewer role, but you can change it as needed.
SSO users count towards your team member limit, so new users can't be added while the team is at its limit.

evidence.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
evidence.text:
When someone logs in through SSO, we will first check if there's an existing team member with a matching email address and SSO configuration. If a match is found, they're logged in as that user. If not, a new user would be created automatically and added to the team whose configured SSO domain matches the email’s domain.

By default, new members are assigned the Viewer role, but you can change it as needed.

SSO users count towards your team member limit, so new users can't be added while the team is at its limit.

A user signing in through SSO can only belong to one team. Team assignment is based on the domain in their email address. Each SSO domain must be unique: a single domain can't be linked to more than one team at once.

You can read more about domains at SSO Domains.

evidence.text:
Our 15% discount is available only to nonprofits, educational institutions and open-source projects choosing a Business plan with annual billing.

## What's included

The discount is 15% off a Business plan with annual billing. Combined with annual billing, you also get 2 months free.

The discount applies to new subscriptions to Business plans with annual billing only. Existing subscriptions, monthly payments and all other plans are excluded.

Your discount continues on renewals for as long as you stay on the same plan. If you upgrade or downgrade your plan for any reason, the discount ends and regular prices apply to your new plan.

## How to apply

1. Start your free 30-day trial. No credit card required.
2. Choose the Business pageview tier you need with annual billing.
3. If you meet the eligibility requirements below and are choosing a Business plan with annual billing, contact us with your organization or project name, type, website and preferred Business pageview tier.
4. We'll send you a discount code to use at checkout.

## Who qualifies

Only nonprofits, educational institutions and open-source projects qualify for this discount. If your organization or project does not fall into one of these categories, it is not eligible.

answer: Yes, you can pin notes to specific dates directly on your traffic chart [1]. If you choose to make the note a site note, it will be visible to all team members who have access to the dashboard, as well as anyone viewing through a shared link [1].

evidence.title: Annotations
evidence.text:
Annotations let you pin notes to specific dates directly on your traffic chart. A product launch, a campaign going live, a site outage, a big press mention: anything that might explain a change in your data.

When you spot a spike or a drop, annotations tell you why it happened. The context is right there on the chart.

## Personal and team annotations

There are two types of annotations:

- **Personal notes** are visible only to you. Use these for notes that are relevant to your own workflow but not worth surfacing to the whole team.
- **Site notes** are visible to all team members who have access to the dashboard, as well as anyone viewing through a shared link.

## Where annotations appear

Annotations show up as markers along the bottom of the main traffic chart. When the date of an annotation falls within your selected time range, the marker appears on the chart. Hover over a marker to read the note attached to it.

Annotations on the traffic chart

## Add an annotation

Hover over the date on the chart where you want to place the annotation. Right-click to open the context menu and select **Add note**. Write a short note describing the event and choose whether it should be personal or shared with your team. Save it and the annotation will appear on the chart immediately.

## Edit or delete an annotation

Hover over the date on the chart where an annotation exists. Right-click to open the context menu and choose to edit the note or delete the annotation entirely. You can always edit or delete your personal annotations. Only team members with editor access or above can add, edit or delete site annotations.

Edit or delete an annotation

## Limits

Each site can have up to 500 annotations. Personal notes and site notes from all team members count towards the same limit. Each note can be up to 255 characters long.

evidence.text:
Buttondown is a minimal and elegant tool for producing newsletters. There's an easy integration with Plausible Analytics, so you can track your Buttondown newsletter to see the traffic numbers of your archives, external link clicks and which of your archive pages drive the most new subscribers.

## How to track newsletter signups

Newsletter signups won’t show up automatically in your Plausible dashboard. You’ll have to configure the goal for them to show up.

To configure a goal, go to your website’s settings in your Plausible Analytics account and visit the **Goals** section. You should see a prompt to add a goal.

Click on the **+ Add goal** button to go to the goal creation form.

Select `Custom event` as the goal trigger and enter this exact name: `Subscribe`.

Add Subscribe goal

Next, click on the **Add goal** button, and you’ll be taken back to the Goals page. After you've completed this process, all the newsletter signups will start being tracked and will be displayed in the **Goals** tab of your Plausible Analytics dashboard.

You'll see **Subscribe** goal as soon as the first subscriber has been tracked. That's all you need to do. Plausible will automatically record new goals (including which page your subscriber is on) whenever you get a new subscriber.

evidence.title: Troubleshooting Plausible Analytics
evidence.text: The Events API returns 202 Accepted even when an event is dropped, usually because `X-Forwarded-For` carries a server IP instead of the visitor's. See debugging the Events API for how to check.

evidence.title: Plausible Events API reference
evidence.text:
The API always returns HTTP 202 Accepted, even when an event is dropped. To debug your setup, there are two tools:

**Check if events are being dropped:** Inspect the response headers for `x-plausible-dropped: 1`. When present, the event was rejected by bot filtering. The most common cause is `X-Forwarded-For` containing a server or CDN IP instead of the actual visitor IP.

**Check which IP address Plausible sees:** Add the `X-Debug-Request: true` header to your request. The API will return HTTP 200 with the IP address it will use for unique visitor counting. Use this to confirm that `X-Forwarded-For` is being forwarded correctly from your proxy. Requests sent with this header are not recorded in your stats, so use it on separate test requests rather than on your real events.

E.g: Add this header to your request and log the response.

**Test the path your real events take.** Send an `X-Debug-Request` test request from the same place your production events are sent (your server, worker, edge function or retry job), not only from your own computer. `X-Forwarded-For` can be set correctly in your code and still reach us with a different IP: a proxy, CDN, load balancer or hosting provider along the way may replace the header or add its own address to it. If the header contains a comma-separated list, Plausible uses the first valid IP address in it, so make sure the visitor's IP comes first. Also check that the visitor's original `User-Agent` is forwarded, not your server's or HTTP library's default.

Dropped events can't be added to your stats afterwards, so it's worth running these checks whenever you set up or change your integration.

Tip: Want to monitor the status of our API?
You can can use GET https://plausible.io/api/health endpoint to do so

evidence.title: Bypass adblockers with a proxy
evidence.text:
When your proxy forwards requests to Plausible, the real visitor IP must be passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. If this header is missing or contains your server's IP instead of the visitor's, Plausible's bot filter will drop the event silently. The API returns HTTP 202 either way.

Most CDN-level proxies such as Cloudflare Workers or Vercel rewrites handle this automatically. If you are writing a custom proxy function, set the header explicitly. If your proxy runs on Cloudflare, also set the `CF-Connecting-IP` header to the visitor's IP address, as Plausible reads it before `X-Forwarded-For`. See the Events API reference for how to verify which IP Plausible is receiving.

Also forward the visitor's `User-Agent`, `Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-CH-UA*`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Pragma` and `Cache-Control` headers. Our bot filter uses them to tell bots from real visitors.

If your CDN or proxy provides the visitor's TLS fingerprint (JA4), forward that header as well.

Make sure your proxy doesn't forward `Cookie`, `Authorization` or any other headers that carry credentials.
